title: Dahal government bans TikTok (November 2023)

description.value: The government of Prime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal banned TikTok in November 2023, saying it disrupted social harmony, goodwill and spread indecent material. The ban was lifted in August and September 2024.

title: Ministry notice: social media platforms must list within three months under the 2080 directive

description.value: Notice posted on the ministry site on 15 Mangsir 2080 (1 Dec 2023) on the Directive for Regulating the Use of Social Media 2080, approved by the cabinet on 2080/7/23 and published in the Nepal Gazette on 2080/08/11. Social media platforms operating at the time of the directive must list with the ministry within three months of the notice and those without an office in Nepal must set up an office or contact point within three months; the ministry may stop operation in Nepal of platforms that do not list. The directive in Nepali and English is said to be on the ministry website.

value.label: Notice on regulating the use of social media, Ministry of Communication and Information Technology (Nepali, 1 December 2023)

issued_by.label: Ministry of Communication and Information Technology

title: Home ministry posts the 2081 procedure for assessing damage from public protests

description.value: Procedure titled "Procedure for assessing damage caused by public demonstrations, strikes and protest programmes, 2081", posted on the MoHA website on 2081-01-18 (1 May 2024). Its provisions could not be read as text.

value.label: Procedure for assessing damage caused by public demonstrations, strikes and protest programmes, 2081 (Nepali)

title: CPJ: arrest of Kantipur Media Group chair appears aimed at muzzling its reporting

description.value: CPJ reported the arrest of Kailash Sirohiya, chair of Kantipur Media Group, over alleged citizenship irregularities, and said it "appears to be an effort to muzzle the critical reporting of Nepal's largest media group".

title: President Paudel appoints Oli prime minister

value.label: K P Sharma Oli appointed Nepal's new Prime Minister

in_response_to.label: Prachanda loses confidence vote in the House of Representatives

title: Oli cabinet of 22 sworn in

description.value: President Paudel administered the oath of office and secrecy to 19 newly appointed ministers; with the prime minister and two deputy prime ministers the cabinet had 22 members. Portfolios include Home (Ramesh Lekhak, Congress), Foreign Affairs (Arzu Rana, Congress), Finance (Deputy PM Bishnu Prasad Paudel, UML), Defence (Manbir Rai) and Communications (Prithvi Subba Gurung, UML).

in_response_to.label: President Paudel appoints Oli prime minister

title: Oli reads out the seven-point Nepali Congress-CPN-UML agreement

value.label: Oli discloses contents of seven-point pact reached between NC, UML

title: Cabinet lifts the TikTok ban

description.value: At a regular Thursday meeting the cabinet decided to lift the ban on TikTok after Prime Minister Oli directed that all social networking sites be treated equally. The decision followed TikTok's assurances to the government.

title: Kathmandu District Court grants five-day remand

description.value: A single bench of judge Ananda Shrestha remanded Oli and Lekhak to five days in custody. Prosecutors had sought 10 days. Lekhak appeared in person; Oli, being treated at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital, appeared virtually. Defence lawyers said there were no grounds for detention.

description.value: A Kathmandu Valley Crime Investigation Office team arrested Chhabi Rijal at his Koteshwor home on Tuesday 31 March 2026, following the Karki commission's recommendations. The Himalayan Times dates the earlier arrests of Oli and Lekhak to 27 March, against 28 March elsewhere.

title: US lowers Nepal travel advisory to Level 2

description.value: The State Department lowered its Nepal advisory to Level 2, "Exercise Increased Caution", citing "an improved security situation following the end of nationwide demonstrations that began in September 2025". It noted that demonstrations "can start with little warning and may quickly turn violent".

title: Supreme Court orders investigation concluded or suspects freed

description.value: On Monday 6 April the Supreme Court ruled that authorities must either formally conclude the investigation or free the suspects, citing health, equal treatment with others released in similar cases, and that the main investigative steps were done.

title: Oli and Lekhak released on condition of availability

description.value: Authorities released Oli and Lekhak on Thursday 9 April after about two weeks of detention, on the condition that they remain available to investigators. Kantipur notes this is release from custody, not from charges. The Kathmandu Post quotes Oli saying he was detained unlawfully for 13 days.

title: Supreme Court full court decides how courts handle case files lost in the 23-24 Bhadra events

description.value: Decision of the Supreme Court full court meeting of 2 Baisakh 2083 (15 Apr 2026) titled "deadlock arising from the events of Bhadra 23 and 24, 2082". The decision sets out how courts should proceed on case files that were destroyed or cannot be recovered, on missing criminal-fine and penalty records, and on seized property, with the first item referring to the 2082 directive on recovery and certification of destroyed case files. A covering letter dated 10 Baisakh 2083 (23 Apr 2026) from the registrar sends the certified decision to all courts.

title: Sudan Gurung resigns as home minister

description.value: Gurung resigned over scrutiny of his financial dealings and alleged ties to a businessman under money-laundering investigation, to allow an impartial investigation. Prime Minister Shah took the Home portfolio in the interim.

description.value: AIG Narayan Dutta Poudel was promoted to Inspector General of the Armed Police Force as Raju Aryal retired. The Karki commission had recommended departmental action against Poudel; the government cited seniority.

description.value: The organisations called for those responsible for violations during the Gen Z protests to be brought to justice, a credible transitional justice process, and release of unpublished official reports on lethal violence against popular movements since 1990.

description.value: The three organisations urged the new government to "bring those responsible for human rights violations during the Gen Z protest to justice" and to complete the transitional justice process in line with international standards.

title: NHRC report recommends legal action and a five-year political ban for Oli and others

description.value: NHRC submitted a report to the government that, according to OCCRP, recommended "sweeping legal action and a five-year political ban" for former Prime Minister Oli, two former ministers and senior security officials, and blamed them for the violence on 8 and 9 September. Himal Press says it identified "the failure of state mechanisms and the excessive use of force by security agencies".

title: NHRC submits report recommending action against Oli and others

description.value: The National Human Rights Commission submitted its report to the government on Wednesday 27 May 2026. It held Oli primarily responsible (his refusal to lift the social media ban was called the direct trigger), also named Ramesh Lekhak and former communications minister Prithvi Subba Gurung, recommended action against named security officers, free lifetime medical treatment for the injured, and, per OCCRP, investigation of 17 RSP lawmakers including Rabi Lamichhane. Himal Press confirms findings of state failure and excessive force but not the named ministers.

description.value: A committee investigating Gurung's finances concluded the allegations could not be substantiated; the Kathmandu Post says it did not consider his landholdings unusual or suspicious, and IANS says it found no established link to the businessman. The report date is not given; the date here is the day of the reappointment reports.

title: Prime Minister Shah addresses the UN General Assembly

description.value: Prime Minister Balendra Shah told the 81st UN General Assembly "Our youth have demanded a politics of integrity and accountability". The retrieved speech text does not name the September 2025 protests or the killings.

title: Regmi committee reports on criminal cases against protesters

description.value: A committee headed by Baburam Regmi reviewed 445 cases naming 1,778 people and advised that charges can be withdrawn only for about 300, because murder, arson and looting cannot be dropped under existing law; 53 cases were already decided by courts. It reported to Home Minister Sudan Gurung on 1 October 2026.

summary.value: From 6 September 2025 TikTok, Reddit and Discord filled with videos and posters announcing a protest on 8 September; AI-generated posters gave "Parliament Building" as the place. title: Gen Z protests in Kathmandu and other cities, 8 September 2025

summary.value: Day-long protests against the social media ban and corruption. A rally began at Maitighar Mandala at about 9 am and moved to New Baneshwar, where it reached the Federal Parliament. Police and armed police used tear gas, water cannon, rubber bullets and live fire; a curfew was imposed from 12:30 pm. Nineteen deaths were reported nationwide by night (17 in Kathmandu, 2 in Itahari) and between 340 and 400+ injured, with protests also in Pokhara, Itahari, Butwal, Bhairahawa, Damak, Biratnagar and Chitwan. The Home Minister resigned that evening and the cabinet lifted the social media ban late that night.

summary.value: After PM Oli resigned on 9 September and the army took security command, Chief of the Army Staff Ashok Raj Sigdel opened talks with Gen Z representatives and other stakeholders at Army Headquarters. summary.value: Protesters set fire to the CPN-UML central office in Chyasal, Lalitpur, on Tuesday afternoon.

part_of.label: Party offices set on fire
Attacks on leaders' homes and party offices

title: Army chief tells foreign military attaches the army is not staging a coup

summary.value: Around 4 pm on 10 September, army officials invited military attaches of Kathmandu embassies to Army Headquarters; Sigdel told them it was not a military takeover. The Kathmandu Post also reports that a young negotiator asked Sigdel whether he was staging a coup that afternoon.

part_of.label: Army-mediated talks on an interim government (9-12 September 2025)

title: Army takes control of Kathmandu

summary.value: Armed soldiers took control of Kathmandu on 10 September, ordering residents indoors under an indefinite curfew; soldiers guarded Parliament while army firefighters worked on the main hall.

title: Gen Z Discord session names Karki for interim prime minister

summary.value: On the Youth Against Corruption Discord server, moderated by Hami Nepal and livestreamed on YouTube, thousands of Gen Z participants debated who should lead an interim government. Karki was chosen: Al Jazeera and Wikipedia give a five-name shortlist (Karki, Timalsina, Dhakal, Sampang, Pun) with Karki on 3,833 of 7,713 votes; The Tribune gives a different runner-up. Timing of the vote is reported inconsistently.

led_to.label: President, army chief and Gen Z representatives hold talks on the interim leader

part_of.label: Army-mediated talks on an interim government (9-12 September 2025)

title: Gen Z groups and Mayor Sampang meet the army chief at Army Headquarters

summary.value: On 10 September, groups claiming to represent Gen Z, and Dharan Mayor Harka Sampang, went to Army Headquarters to talk to Chief of the Army Staff Sigdel. One group left after Sigdel asked them to sit with Durga Prasai and representatives of the Rastriya Swatantra Party. Crowds outside chanted different names (Karki, Balen Shah, Harka Sampang) and soldiers told them to agree among themselves and return the next day.

led_to.label: President, army chief and Gen Z representatives hold talks on the interim leader

part_of.label: Army-mediated talks on an interim government (9-12 September 2025)

title: Oli says in a letter that he is at the Shivapuri army camp

summary.value: On the night of 10 September, KP Sharma Oli addressed a letter to "Dear Gen Z kids" stating that he was at the Shivapuri barracks, denying reports that he had fled the country. Setopati reported that Oli, Pushpa Kamal Dahal, Madhav Kumar Nepal and several ministers had been kept at the army centre for their safety.

title: Army eases curfew and prohibitory orders in Kathmandu Valley

summary.value: On 11 September the army shortened the prohibitory order (10 am to 5 pm) and kept the curfew from 7 pm to 6 am, allowing essential services and ticketed air travellers to move. Euronews reported the curfew as briefly lifted on Thursday; Al Jazeera said the nationwide curfew first imposed on Tuesday night would stay in place until Friday.

title: Gen Z leaders hold a press conference backing Karki and demanding dissolution

summary.value: ANI reports that on Thursday 11 September leaders of the Gen Z protest endorsed Karki at a press conference, citing her integrity and independence. PTI reports Gen Z leaders saying at a press meet that parliament must be dissolved and the constitution amended. AFP quotes Sudan Gurung telling reporters on Thursday that their "first demand is the dissolution of parliament".

part_of.label: Army-mediated talks on an interim government (9-12 September 2025)

title: Night consultations with party leaders at Sheetal Niwas

summary.value: From Thursday night into Friday morning talks at Sheetal Niwas ended without resolution. President Paudel invited Maoist Centre chairman Pushpa Kamal Dahal on Thursday evening and Congress leaders were contacted by phone around 11 pm. Parties signalled support for Karki but wanted parliament kept.

led_to.label: Friday talks at Sheetal Niwas agree on Karki and dissolution

part_of.label: Army-mediated talks on an interim government (9-12 September 2025)

title: President, army chief and Gen Z representatives hold talks on the interim leader

summary.value: On Thursday 11 September, President Paudel and Chief of the Army Staff Sigdel were due to talk to Gen Z representatives under army coordination. Reports differ on what stalled the talks: who should lead the interim government (ETV Bharat) or the constitutional route and dissolution of parliament (Nepali Times). The venue moved from Army Headquarters to the President's Sheetal Niwas on Thursday.

led_to.label: Friday talks at Sheetal Niwas agree on Karki and dissolution

part_of.label: Army-mediated talks on an interim government (9-12 September 2025)

title: Ramechhap District Prison clash

summary.value: Nepal Army personnel opened fire during a clash at Ramechhap District Prison when inmates tried to break out, demanding to go home. Reports give 12 or 13 injured. The number of inmates killed is two in Himalaya Press and the Himalayan Times and three in PTI.

part_of.label: Prison breaks

title: House of Representatives dissolved and election set for 5 March 2026

summary.value: Parliament was dissolved with effect from 11 pm on 12 September under a notification of the President's Office, on the recommendation of the interim government approved at Karki's first cabinet meeting. President Paudel announced fresh elections for 5 March 2026. Nepali Congress, CPN-UML and Maoist Centre called the dissolution unconstitutional.

led_to.label: Curfew and prohibitory orders lifted in Kathmandu Valley

title: Sushila Karki sworn in as interim prime minister

summary.value: President Ram Chandra Paudel administered the oath to former Chief Justice Sushila Karki, 73, as interim prime minister on Friday night; she is Nepal's first woman prime minister. The presidential press adviser announced the swearing-in for 9 pm; B360 posted that she was appointed at 9:20 pm. Her oath was broadcast on state television.

led_to.label: House of Representatives dissolved and election set for 5 March 2026

part_of.label: Army-mediated talks on an interim government (9-12 September 2025)

title: Sushila Karki appointed interim prime minister

summary.value: Sushila Karki, a former chief justice, took charge of an interim government on 12 September 2025 (HRW, UN News).

title: Friday talks at Sheetal Niwas agree on Karki and dissolution

summary.value: On Friday 12 September, after a meeting postponed from 9 am, the President, army chief, Chief Justice Prakash Man Singh Raut, Maoist Centre leaders, Gen Z representatives and constitutional experts reached agreement: Karki as interim prime minister and dissolution of the House of Representatives. Sudan Gurung reportedly insisted on dissolution first; the army chief reportedly warned an emergency might be declared if no government was in place by evening.

led_to.label: Sushila Karki sworn in as interim prime minister

part_of.label: Army-mediated talks on an interim government (9-12 September 2025)

title: Curfew and prohibitory orders lifted in Kathmandu Valley

summary.value: On Saturday 13 September the Nepal Army lifted the curfew and restrictive orders in Kathmandu Valley and other parts of Nepal; shops and markets reopened and cleaning drives began, though sensitive areas stayed off-limits.

title: PM Karki visits injured protesters in hospitals

summary.value: On Saturday 13 September Karki visited Bir Hospital, the Trauma Centre and Civil Service Hospital at New Baneshwar to see young people injured in the protests.

title: Rabi Lamichhane returns to Nakkhu Prison

summary.value: Republica reports Lamichhane returned to Nakkhu on Saturday evening, 13 September, after the prison issued a notice requiring all absconding inmates to return or face further charges.

part_of.label: Prison breaks

title: Sudan Gurung's group protests at the PM's residence over the cabinet

summary.value: On Sunday night 14 September, a group led by Sudan Gurung protested in front of the prime minister's residence in Baluwatar, saying the cabinet expansion was done without consulting them and demanding Karki's resignation. Gurung said of Om Prakash Aryal "he's making himself home minister from inside!".

title: Karki consults aides and Gen Z leaders on the cabinet

summary.value: On 13-14 September Karki started consultations with aides and Gen Z leaders to form a cabinet of under 15 ministers. Gen Z members also held consultations on Discord. Names circulating included Om Prakash Aryal, Kulman Ghising and doctors Bhagawan Koirala and Sanduk Ruit. Hami Nepal leaders reportedly refused to join the government.

led_to.label: First three ministers sworn in: Khanal, Ghising and Aryal

title: Karki takes charge of the Prime Minister's Office at Singha Durbar

summary.value: Karki took charge of her office in the Singha Durbar complex on Sunday 14 September (scheduled for 11 am per ANI) and held a minute of silence for those killed. In a first address she said "We will not stay here more than six months in any situation".

led_to.label: First three ministers sworn in: Khanal, Ghising and Aryal

title: First three ministers sworn in: Khanal, Ghising and Aryal

summary.value: On Monday 15 September President Paudel administered the oath to Rameshwor Khanal (finance), Kulman Ghising (energy, water resources and irrigation, plus infrastructure and transport and urban development) and Om Prakash Aryal (home affairs, plus law, justice and parliamentary affairs) at a ceremony in front of the ruins of Sheetal Niwas.

title: Oli leaves army protection

summary.value: KP Sharma Oli, who had stayed at the army staff college in Shivapuri since 9 September, left on Thursday 18 September; sources told Setopati that he had started living in a rented house in the Gundu area of Bhaktapur. A UML publicity chief said the party had no information on where he stayed.

title: Five more ministers named and inquiry commission formed

summary.value: On Sunday 21 September Karki recommended five ministers (Anil Kumar Sinha, Mahabir Pun, Madan Prasad Pariyar, Jagdish Kharel, Sangeeta Mishra) and the cabinet formed a judicial inquiry commission under Gauri Bahadur Karki. ANI reports four ministers sworn in on Monday 22 September.

title: More than 6,800 escaped prisoners still at large

summary.value: On 25 September 2025 officials said more than 6,800 people who escaped prisons and custody during the unrest remained at large; the director of the Department of Prison Management is quoted on the number rearrested. The numbers inside the one retrieved article are not consistent with each other (about 6,900 rearrested against about 7,300 recaptured).

title: Forensic report: live bullets killed protesters

summary.value: Reuters reported that at least 33 protesters were struck by live bullets from high-velocity firearms, per the Tribhuvan University Institute of Medicine's forensic department; of 34 bodies with bullet wounds, only one had a rubber bullet wound.

involved.label: Tribhuvan University Institute of Medicine, forensic medicine department

title: Ten left parties merge into the Nepali Communist Party

summary.value: Ten left parties, including the CPN (Maoist Centre), merged into the Nepali Communist Party with Pushpa Kamal Dahal as coordinator and Madhav Kumar Nepal as co-coordinator. The Tribune ties the merger to the September uprising and the announced March elections. CPN-UML stayed out.

title: Gen Z activists and police clash at Simara Chowk, Bara

summary.value: Six Gen Z youths were injured in a clash after Gen Z activists protested at Simara Chowk in Bara. Police arrested three people, including two ward chairs elected from UML; three others remained at large. Gen Z leaders accused police of security lapses. A six-point verbal deal followed at the Armed Police Force Technical School in Pathahiya.

title: HRW report on unlawful use of force

summary.value: Human Rights Watch published an analysis of 50 verified videos and other evidence on the 8 and 9 September violence.

title: Gen Z groups demand interim PM Karki's resignation

summary.value: Onlinekhabar reports protesters chanting for Prime Minister Sushila Karki to resign outside Baluwatar, a riot-police charge on organisers, and a petition by 23 Gen Z groups to the President asking for her removal for sidelining the movement's core demands. It also reports an allegation of nepotism against her chief private secretary.

title: RSP and Bibeksheel Sajha announce merger

summary.value: The Rastriya Swatantra Party, led by Rabi Lamichhane, and the Bibeksheel Sajha Party, headed by Samiksha Baskota, announced their merger on 30 November 2025. The unified party keeps the RSP name and the bell symbol.

title: Amnesty report on unlawful killings

summary.value: Amnesty International published findings that security forces used unnecessary and excessive force, based on verified eyewitness accounts, photographic and video evidence and interviews.

title: Oli re-elected CPN-UML chair at 11th general convention

summary.value: KP Sharma Oli was re-elected CPN-UML chairman at the party's 11th general convention with 1,663 votes against Ishwar Pokhrel's 564. Polling began on Wednesday 17 December and ended early on Thursday 18 December.

title: Election Commission publishes final voters' roll

summary.value: The Election Commission published the final voters' roll with 18,903,689 eligible voters, 915,119 more than in 2022, and designated 10,967 polling stations for the 5 March 2026 election.

led_to.label: House of Representatives election

title: Ujyaalo Nepal Party splits from RSP

summary.value: The Ujyaalo Nepal Party, widely considered Kulman Ghising's creation, formally split from the RSP on Saturday 10 January 2026, 12 days after the two parties announced unity under a seven-point agreement on 29 December 2025. The Kathmandu Post gives disagreement over distribution of portfolios as the sole reason.

title: Nepali Congress special convention elects Gagan Thapa president

summary.value: A special general convention elected Gagan Thapa Nepali Congress president as the only candidate on 14 January 2026. The same day the Deuba-aligned committee suspended Thapa and Bishwa Prakash Sharma for five years. The Election Commission recognised the Thapa-led party on 16 January; the Deuba camp said it would contest this.

title: Oli denies giving a firing order

summary.value: KP Sharma Oli said he had not given an order to fire, and that no force was used at the Maitighar demonstration.

title: BBC investigation published

summary.value: BBC investigation, reported 26 and 27 February 2026, says a police call sign 'Peter 1', identified as former IGP Chandra Kuber Khapung, ordered use of necessary force; it draws on over 4,000 videos and photographs, police radio logs and security officials' reports.

title: House of Representatives election

summary.value: Election to the 275-member House of Representatives, the first since the September 2025 uprising, held on the date set on 12 September 2025. Turnout was about 60 per cent. The RSP won 125 of 165 direct seats and 57 proportional seats, 182 in total; Nepali Congress 38; CPN-UML 25. Balendra Shah beat Oli in Jhapa-5 by 49,614 votes. Interim counts and analyst estimates ran ahead of the final total (an estimate of 185-190 seats on 9 March; 119 direct seats at an interim count).

led_to.label: Balendra Shah sworn in as prime minister

title: Karki commission submits report on 8-9 September events

summary.value: The three-member commission chaired by Gauri Bahadur Karki handed its report to Prime Minister Sushila Karki on Sunday 8 March 2026, after questioning about 200 people. Outlets give different lengths (1,000 pages; 8,000-10,000 pages). The report recommended criminal investigation of Oli, Lekhak and Khapung under Sections 181 and 182, and departmental action against police, Armed Police and Army officers. After outlets published its content, Karki decided on about 25 March to release it formally.

involved.label: Commission investigating the 8-9 September 2025 events (Karki commission)
Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers

led_to.label: Former PM Oli and former Home Minister Lekhak arrested
Commission report on Bhadra 23 and 24 incidents

title: Commission report on Bhadra 23 and 24 incidents

summary.value: Commission of inquiry report on the 8 and 9 September events, reported as under cabinet review on 9 March 2026. It analysed CCTV and audio-visual material, a criminal investigation of Oli, Lekhak and Khapung was recommended (Kantipur headline), and the report records party-cadre involvement in arson (Ratopati).

involved.label: Commission investigating the 8-9 September 2025 events (Karki commission)

title: Balendra Shah sworn in as prime minister

summary.value: President Ram Chandra Paudel swore in Balendra Shah (35, RSP) as prime minister on Friday 27 March 2026. Fourteen ministers took the oath at the ceremony, with Sudan Gurung as home minister. Sushila Karki had left office the same week.

led_to.label: Former PM Oli and former Home Minister Lekhak arrested

title: Former PM Oli and former Home Minister Lekhak arrested

summary.value: Nepal Police arrested Oli and Lekhak early on Saturday 28 March 2026 from their homes in Bhaktapur, after the new cabinet decided to implement the commission report, in a case of negligence leading to deaths on 8 September 2025. Outlets differ on whether the warrants were issued by a court or were urgent warrants awaiting validation, and on the Penal Code sections.

title: UML secretariat meeting debates Oli's leadership

summary.value: At a UML secretariat meeting reported on 24 May 2026, Yogesh Bhattarai said the party could not move forward under Oli and that he should resign (reported indirectly by Spotlight Nepal).

led_to.label: UML vice-chair and general secretary submit opposing reports on Oli

title: Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods

summary.value: Floods on the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers in August 2026. By 5 October 2026 the government had suspended search and rescue except in emergencies and was moving to reconstruction. Not linked in the sources to the September 2025 protests; recorded because it is the main current crisis in the dataset's final weeks.

responded_by.label: National Council for Disaster Risk Reduction and Management

title: First anniversary: Gen Z Martyrs' Day

summary.value: Nepal observed 8 September 2026 as Gen Z Martyrs' Day, a public holiday. A programme by the GenZ Martyrs' Family Welfare Society in New Baneshwor was attended by the Home Minister, ministers and families. Hamro Patro says 76 people died and the government has declared 45 martyrs; embassies including Australia, Norway, the UK, the US and Japan posted messages. An injured protester told Africanews the injured still needed state support.

led_to.label: Parties issue contrasting statements on the anniversary

title: Parties issue contrasting statements on the anniversary

summary.value: On 8-9 September 2026 the RSP and Lamichhane stressed state repression and the spontaneity of the movement; Oli described the 9 September destruction as the result of a planned attempt; Pushpa Kamal Dahal said the two days should not be viewed the same way; Gagan Thapa sent a video tribute. IANS summarises that the RSP played down property destruction while opposition parties stressed it.

title: UML vice-chair and general secretary submit opposing reports on Oli

summary.value: Vice-chair Ram Bahadur Thapa's 39-page report defended Oli and said losing an election does not require the chair to resign. General Secretary Shankar Pokharel's 65-page report recommended Oli step down.

title: Nepali Congress 15th general convention

summary.value: Leaders of the Congress, RSP, Nepali Communist Party and UML spoke at the Congress general convention at Khula Manch (Tundikhel), pledging cooperation on democracy and the constitution. Gagan Thapa criticised the prime minister's absence from Parliament; Dahal and UML's Pokharel raised fears of authoritarianism. Thapa's interview of the same date places the start on 6 October and refers to a parallel convention by Sher Bahadur Deuba.

A ProPakistani report also covered it. Alt News adds signage in the clip: 'Total PARCO' on a fuel station, a Pakistani joint venture, and 'Royal Kulfi', a shop with stores across Lahore. title: Cooperative savings fraud victims

description.value: Depositors in fraudulent savings cooperatives who have protested repeatedly in Kathmandu, mostly on the Maitighar-Baneshwar stretch, demanding return of their money. The Kathmandu Post counts more than 2,000 victims filing complaints against 123 cooperatives owing over Rs960 million.

title: CPN (Maoist Centre)

description.value: Party chaired by Pushpa Kamal Dahal. Dissolved on 4 November 2025 when its central committee merged it with other communist parties into the Nepali Communist Party. Headquarters: Perisdanda, Koteshwor, Kathmandu (Wikipedia).

title: CPN-UML

description.value: Communist Party of Nepal (Unified Marxist-Leninist). Chaired by KP Sharma Oli since 2014. Won 79 seats in the 2022 election, the second largest party. Wikipedia lists its headquarters at Thapathali, Kathmandu, and reports that protesters vandalised the headquarters in September 2025.

title: CPN (Unified Socialist)

description.value: Party named by Setopati as the party of former prime minister Jhalanath Khanal when his wife was injured on 9 September 2025.

title: Cyabra

description.value: Cyber intelligence company based in Tel Aviv, Israel, that analyses online disinformation and fake accounts.

title: Dainik Bhaskar

description.value: Indian Hindi daily. Alt News says its national editor shared an Indonesian protest video as showing Nepal.

title: Department of Prison Management

description.value: Government body that gave the prisoner escape and return figures cited in the reporting on the September 2025 jail breaks.

title: Dharan Sub-Metropolitan City

description.value: Local government of Dharan, eastern Nepal; Harka Sampang was mayor from 23 May 2022 to 19 January 2026 (Wikipedia).

title: Digital Rights Nepal

description.value: Rights group whose president, Bhola Nath Dhungana, criticised the 4 September 2025 closure as a hit on fundamental rights.

title: Discord

description.value: Chat platform (Discord Inc., San Francisco, founded May 2015). On the list of 26 blocked platforms; Wikipedia reports it was nevertheless used in the 2025 Nepal protests to coordinate and to help choose a new prime minister.

title: District Administration Office, Kathmandu

description.value: Office of the Chief District Officer of Kathmandu; it issued the curfew order of 9 September 2025 under CDO Chhabi Rijal (Deccan Herald).

title: District Administration Office, Lalitpur

description.value: Office of the Chief District Officer of Lalitpur, Suman Ghimire, which applied the 9 September 2025 curfew to parts of wards 2, 4, 9, 18 and 25.

title: Election Commission of Nepal

description.value: Constitutional body founded 12 November 1951, headquartered at Kantipath, Kathmandu; it recognised Gagan Thapa's leadership of the Nepali Congress on 16 January 2026 (Himal Press).

title: Embassy of Finland in Nepal

description.value: Finnish diplomatic mission. Listed as a signatory of the joint statement of 9 September 2025.

title: Embassy of France in Nepal

description.value: French diplomatic mission. Listed as a signatory of the joint statement of 9 September 2025.

title: Embassy of Germany in Nepal

description.value: German diplomatic mission. Listed as a signatory of the joint statement of 9 September 2025 by Diplomat Nepal only (B360 Nepal lists seven missions without Germany).

title: Embassy of Japan in Nepal

description.value: Japanese diplomatic mission. Listed as a signatory of the joint statement of 9 September 2025.

title: Embassy of Norway in Nepal

description.value: Norwegian diplomatic mission. Listed as a signatory of the joint statement of 9 September 2025 by Diplomat Nepal only (B360 Nepal lists seven missions without Norway).

title: Embassy of the Republic of Korea in Nepal

description.value: South Korean diplomatic mission. Listed as a signatory of the joint statement of 9 September 2025.

title: European Union Delegation to Nepal

description.value: EU mission in Kathmandu; Ambassador Veronique Lorenzo welcomed Karki's appointment.

title: Everest Hospital

description.value: Hospital in New Baneshwar named in reporting as having received dead or dying protesters on 8 September 2025.

title: Facebook (Meta Platforms)

description.value: Facebook is a product of Meta Platforms (founded 4 February 2004, headquartered in Menlo Park, California), which also owns Instagram, WhatsApp and Threads. Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger were on the list of 26 platforms blocked in Nepal on 4 September 2025.

title: Federal Parliament of Nepal

description.value: Bicameral legislature. Both houses met at the International Convention Centre, New Baneshwor, until September 2025, when protesters stormed and burned the building; the lower house now meets in a new Parliament House within the Singha Durbar premises (Wikipedia).

title: Federation of Nepali Journalists

description.value: Professional journalists' association; its website lists membership of the International Federation of Journalists and IFEX (accessed 2026-10-05).

title: International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH)

description.value: International human rights federation. Co-signed a statement on 9 September 2025 with OMCT, FORUM-ASIA, CIVICUS and nine Nepali civil society organisations, and the 12-13 September joint statement.

title: Federation of Nepalese Chambers of Commerce and Industry

description.value: Private-sector federation. Its president gave a preliminary private-sector loss estimate of NPR 80 to 100 billion to Prime Minister Sushila Karki on 21 September 2025.

title: Freedom Forum

description.value: Nepali NGO working on democracy, human rights, press freedom, freedom of expression and the right to information; its site says it was established in February 2005 by media professionals, legal experts and academics.

title: Gauri Bahadur Karki inquiry commission

description.value: Commission led by former judge Gauri Bahadur Karki that reported on the Gen Z protests; reporting says it largely stays silent on the second day of violence.

title: GenZ Martyrs' Family Welfare Society

description.value: Society that organised a programme in New Baneshwor on 8 September 2026, attended by the Home Minister, other ministers and families of the dead.

title: Gen Z movement (Nepal, 2025)

description.value: Loose network of youth groups, including Hami Nepal, that led the September 2025 protests and sent representatives to the army-mediated talks. Reports show several groups with different preferred interim leaders.

title: Commission investigating the 8-9 September 2025 events (Karki commission)

description.value: Government-appointed commission chaired by retired Supreme Court judge Gauri Bahadur Karki. It handed its report to Prime Minister Sushila Karki on 8 March 2026 and recommended criminal investigation of Oli, Lekhak and IGP Khapung and action against other officials (Onlinekhabar, 25 March 2026).

title: Gorkha Media Network

description.value: Media company where Rabi Lamichhane was managing director; a parliamentary committee concluded cooperative funds were funnelled into it. An audit report cited by the Kathmandu Post counts Rs109.936 million deposited into its accounts.

title: Hami Nepal

description.value: Youth-led NGO founded by Sudan Gurung, known for earthquake relief. Wikipedia reports it called the 8 September 2025 protest, used Discord and Instagram to coordinate, worked with about 140 influencers, and met army leadership after Oli's resignation.

title: The Himalayan Times

description.value: English-language daily founded 23 November 2001, owned by International Media Network Nepal. Wikipedia reports that the Press Council Nepal blacklisted it in 2025 after a complaint about its reporting, which the paper disputed.

title: Hotel Association Nepal

description.value: Trade body that reported hotel-sector losses from the September 2025 protests.

title: House of Representatives of Nepal

description.value: Lower house of the Federal Parliament, 275 seats. Dissolved on 12 September 2025; election held on 5 March 2026, in which the Rastriya Swatantra Party won 182 seats.

title: Human Rights Watch

description.value: International rights organisation. Its report of 19 November 2025 says researchers analysed and verified 50 videos from 8 September.

title: IBC24

description.value: Indian regional news channel. Decode reports it claimed Oli left a secret resignation letter.

title: India Today

description.value: Indian news group. BOOM names it among outlets that reported the death of Ravi Laxmi Chitrakar.

title: INSEC

description.value: Informal Sector Service Centre, a Nepali human rights organisation that runs INSEC Online, a human rights news portal; it published a statement condemning the use of force in the protests.

title: Instagram

description.value: Meta-owned platform. Named by the Kathmandu Post among the platforms that did not apply to register by the deadline and were blocked from 4 September 2025. Hami Nepal used its Instagram account to circulate protest information.

title: International Commission of Jurists (ICJ)

description.value: International jurists' organisation. Published and co-signed joint statements on 13 September 2025 and 12-13 February 2026.

title: Internet Service Providers Association of Nepal

description.value: Industry body that the NTA instructed to enforce the blocking, according to Swarajya.

title: Janata Samajwadi Party, Nepal

description.value: Founded 22 April 2020; chaired by Upendra Yadav. Won 12 of 275 seats in 2022. Several factions split from it between 2021 and 2025. Wikipedia's English title for the party is People's Socialist Party, Nepal (2020); a different party founded in 2024 by Ashok Rai uses a similar name.

title: Embassy of Japan in Kathmandu

description.value: Welcomed Karki's appointment as an important step in Nepal's transition, in a Facebook statement reported by The Himalayan Times via The Tribune.

title: Judicial inquiry commission on the 8-9 September 2025 events

description.value: Commission formed by the Karki cabinet on 21 September 2025 under the Commission of Inquiry Act, led by Gauri Bahadur Karki, with three months to report.

part_of_org.label: Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers

title: Kantipur Media Group

description.value: Publisher founded in 1993 (Kantipur Publications Pvt. Ltd.), chaired by Kailash Sirohiya; outlets include the Kantipur daily, The Kathmandu Post, Kantipur Television and Kantipur FM. During the Gen Z protests demonstrators forced staff from its headquarters and set fire to one building, per Wikipedia.

title: Kaski District Administration Office

description.value: Imposed an indefinite prohibitory order in Pokhara from 2 pm on 8 September 2025.

title: Kathmandu Central Jail

description.value: Prison in Dillibazar, Kathmandu, as located in OpenStreetMap; Wikipedia's account of the protests lists the Kathmandu main prison among the prisons where a breakout was reported thwarted.

title: Kathmandu District Court

description.value: District court that remanded Durga Prasai and an associate to 12 days of judicial custody on 11 April 2025.

title: Kathmandu District Security Committee

description.value: District committee that met on 7 September 2025 and concluded the overall security situation was normal, per Onlinekhabar.

title: Kathmandu Medical College Teaching Hospital

description.value: Hospital in Sinamangal named in reporting as having received dead or dying protesters on 8 September 2025.

title: Kathmandu Metropolitan City

description.value: Local government of Kathmandu; Balendra Shah was its mayor from 30 May 2022 to 18 January 2026, then Sunita Dangol acted as mayor (Wikipedia).

title: The Kathmandu Post

description.value: English-language daily founded in February 1993, owned by Kantipur Media Group; editor-in-chief Biswas Baral.

title: LinkedIn

description.value: Professional network. Named among the platforms that did not apply to register and were blocked from 4 September 2025.

title: Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development

description.value: Ministry headed by Ram Nath Adhikari until his resignation on 9 September 2025.

title: Ministry of Communication and Information Technology

description.value: Ministry whose directive led the Nepal Telecommunications Authority to publish a list of 26 platforms to be shut down in September 2025 (Kathmandu Post). Prithvi Subba Gurung was its minister from 15 July 2024 to 9 September 2025. Its website could not be fetched (certificate error).

title: Ministry of Defence

description.value: Located at Singha Durbar. Minister of Defence from 15 July 2024 to 9 September 2025 was Manbir Rai; its website lists the Prime Minister as also Defence Minister (accessed 2026-10-05).

title: Ministry of Education

description.value: Ministry led in the fourth Oli cabinet by CPN-UML's Bidya Bhattarai from 15 July 2024 to 21 April 2025.

title: Ministry of Education, Science and Technology

description.value: Ministry led by Mahabir Pun in the Karki interim cabinet, 22 September 2025 to 20 January 2026.

title: Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation

description.value: Ministry held by Kulman Ghising from 15 September 2025 to 7 January 2026 (Karki interim cabinet).

title: Ministry of External Affairs (India)

description.value: Indian foreign ministry. Issued a statement on 9 September 2025 on developments in Nepal and an advisory to Indian nationals.

title: Ministry of Finance

description.value: Ministry headed in the Oli cabinet by Deputy Prime Minister Bishnu Prasad Paudel, in the Karki interim cabinet by Rameshwor Khanal and since 27 March 2026 by Swarnim Wagle.

title: Ministry of Foreign Affairs

description.value: Located at Singha Durbar, Kathmandu. Its website names Shisir Khanal as minister (accessed 2026-10-05).

title: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (China)

description.value: Chinese foreign ministry. Its spokesperson commented on Nepal on 10 September 2025.

title: Ministry of Health and Population

description.value: Ministry reported to have instructed hospitals to give free treatment to injured protesters on 8 September 2025.

title: Ministry of Home Affairs

description.value: Ministry that oversees Nepal Police and the Armed Police Force. Its website lists Sudhan (Sudan) Gurung as minister (accessed 2026-10-05).

title: Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs

description.value: Ministry held by Om Prakash Aryal from 15 to 22 September 2025, then by Anil Kumar Sinha.

title: Ministry of Urban Development

description.value: Ministry headed by Deputy Prime Minister Prakash Man Singh in the fourth Oli cabinet.

title: Ministry of Water Supply

description.value: Ministry headed by Pradip Yadav, who resigned on 9 September 2025.

title: Ministry of Youth and Sports

description.value: Ministry headed by Tejulal Chaudhary, who resigned on 9 September 2025.

title: Nakkhu Prison

description.value: Prison in Lalitpur established in 1950. Rabi Lamichhane was freed from Nakkhu prison on 9 September 2025 when protesters entered the facility (Wikipedia); he was later held there again until his bail on 19 December 2025 (Himal Press).

title: National Assembly of Nepal

description.value: Upper house of Nepal's federal parliament, where the Social Media Bill was introduced in early 2025.

title: National Council for Disaster Risk Reduction and Management

description.value: Council chaired by Prime Minister Balendra Shah. In early October 2026 it recommended a Rs559.17 billion budget for 504 reconstruction plans after the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods.

title: National Investigation Department

description.value: Nepal’s intelligence agency under the Prime Minister’s Office. Onlinekhabar reports it filed a six-point report on the Gen Z movement on 7 September 2025.

title: NDTV

description.value: Indian news broadcaster. Alt News and Decode report that NDTV channels aired old Pashupatinath Temple footage as an attack by protesters; BOOM lists NDTV among outlets that reported the death of Ravi Laxmi Chitrakar.

title: Nepal Bar Association

description.value: Lawyers' association founded in 1956 with headquarters on Ram Shah Path, Kathmandu.

title: Nepal Electricity Authority

description.value: State electricity utility; Kulman Ghising was its managing director from 2016 to 2020 and from 2021 until his removal on 24 March 2025 (Wikipedia).

title: Nepal Insurance Authority

description.value: Insurance regulator that reported claim totals from the September 2025 protest damage.

title: Nepal Police

description.value: National police force founded in 1955, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, headquartered at Naxal, Kathmandu, with 79,541 employees (Wikipedia). Inspector General: Chandra Kuber Khapung from 4 September 2025, then Dan Bahadur Karki.

title: Nepal Police Hospital

description.value: Hospital in Maharajgunj, Kathmandu, opened in 2040 BS (1983-84) for police personnel and families, now 400 beds and open to the public.

title: Nepal Telecommunications Authority

description.value: Autonomous telecom regulator established in 1998 under the Telecommunications Act 1997. Following the ministry's directive it published the list of 26 platforms to be shut down in September 2025 (Kathmandu Post, 5 September 2025).

title: Nepali Army

description.value: National army, headquartered at Jangi Adda, Bhadrakali, Kathmandu; Chief of the Army Staff is General Ashok Raj Sigdel (96,500 active personnel, 2026, Wikipedia).

title: Nepali Communist Party

description.value: Formed on 5 November 2025 by merging the CPN (Maoist Centre), CPN (Unified Socialist) and other communist groups, not CPN-UML. Coordinator Pushpa Kamal Dahal; co-coordinator Madhav Kumar Nepal; Jhalanath Khanal ranked third. Won 17 of 275 seats in 2026 (Wikipedia).

title: Nepali Congress

description.value: Party founded on 9 April 1950. Gagan Thapa has been president since January 2026, after Sher Bahadur Deuba's tenure that began in 2016. Won 89 seats in 2022 and 38 in 2026. Headquarters: B.P. Smriti Bhawan, Lalitpur (Wikipedia).

title: News18

description.value: Indian news broadcaster. Decode reports it framed the protest with a Hindu nation angle and carried a claim of a secret Oli resignation letter; BOOM lists it among outlets that reported the death of Ravi Laxmi Chitrakar.

title: National Human Rights Commission, Nepal

description.value: Constitutional human rights body chaired by Top Bahadur Magar since 3 February 2021. Its report on the protest killings, reported on 27 May 2026, held Oli primarily responsible and recommended action against Lekhak, Prithvi Subba Gurung and senior police officers.

title: Office of the President of Nepal

description.value: Office and official residence of the President of Nepal at Shital Niwas (Rashtrapati Bhavan), Maharajgunj. The Kathmandu Post calls Shital Niwas 'the President's office'.

title: Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers

description.value: Executive office of the Government of Nepal at Singha Durbar, Kathmandu. Its website names Balendra Shah as Prime Minister (accessed 2026-10-05).

title: OHCHR

description.value: Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, established 20 December 1993; Volker Türk has been High Commissioner since 17 October 2022.

title: World Organisation Against Torture (OMCT)

description.value: International network against torture. Co-signatory of the 9 September 2025 statement on the protest crackdown.

title: Online Khabar

description.value: Independent online news portal founded in 2006 with Nepali and English editions; founder and president Dharma Raj Bhusal.

title: Parliamentary special committee on cooperative fraud

description.value: Parliamentary special inquiry committee whose report concluded Rabi Lamichhane was involved in misuse of cooperative funds.

title: Pathao

description.value: Ride-hailing and delivery company. Its then managing director, Asheem Man Singh Basnyat, said he would join the 8 September 2025 protest at Maitighar.

title: Pinterest

description.value: Image-sharing platform. Named by the Guardian and Swarajya among the blocked platforms.

title: Pragatisheel Loktantrik Party

description.value: Party led by Baburam Bhattarai from 20 November 2025, formed in the split of the CPN (Maoist Centre) (Wikipedia pages on Bhattarai and the Maoist Centre).

title: High-level study committee on cases against Gen Z protesters

description.value: Committee headed by former High Court judge Baburam Regmi, with former Deputy Attorney General Chet Nath Ghimire and retired DIG Poshraj Pokharel. It submitted its report to Home Minister Sudan Gurung on 1 October 2026.

title: Rastriya Prajatantra Party

description.value: Founded 29 May 1990; chaired by Rajendra Lingden since December 2021. Won 14 seats in 2022 and 5 in 2026, losing national party status (Wikipedia).

title: Rastriya Swatantra Party

description.value: Founded 1 July 2022; chaired by Rabi Lamichhane. Won 21 seats in 2022 and 182 of 275 in the March 2026 election (47.84% of the proportional vote). Balen Shah leads the parliamentary party and became Prime Minister on 27 March 2026. Headquarters: Chamati, Kathmandu (Wikipedia).

title: Reddit

description.value: Forum platform founded 23 June 2005 in San Francisco. Reddit is on the Kathmandu Post list of the 26 platforms blocked on 4 September 2025.

title: Reporters Without Borders (RSF)

description.value: Press freedom organisation. Statements on the Social Media Bill (June 2025) and on media outlets and journalists attacked on 8 and 9 September 2025.

title: Republic TV

description.value: Indian news channel. Named by Newslaundry for saying the protest was a CIA plot, and by BOOM among outlets that reported the death of Ravi Laxmi Chitrakar.

title: Rupandehi District Administration Office

description.value: Imposed a curfew order in the Butwal-Bhairahawa area from 4 pm to 10 pm on 8 September 2025.

title: Committee to study security agencies' role on 8-9 September

description.value: Committee formed by the cabinet on 15 April 2026 under former High Court judge Prem Raj Karki, with former APF AIG Subodh Adhikari and former police AIG Tek Prasad Rai, to study the inquiry findings and security mechanisms.

title: Shram Sanskriti Party

description.value: Party founded by Harka Sampang, the former mayor of Dharan (Wikipedia).

title: sidhakura.com

description.value: News website whose publisher and executive editor were convicted of contempt by a Supreme Court extended full bench, the case in which the Court said online and social media platforms must register.

title: Signal

description.value: Messaging app. Named by the Guardian and Swarajya among the blocked platforms.

title: Special Task Force (Nepal Police)

description.value: Unit named as having fired from inside the Parliament compound on 8 September 2025. The Kathmandu Post names it only as the Special Task Force; Human Rights Watch calls it the Nepal Police's Special Task Force.

title: Sunsari District Administration Office

description.value: District administration of Sunsari, where Itahari is located. Reporting says a curfew was implemented in Itahari on 8 September 2025.

title: Supreme Court of Nepal

description.value: Apex court, a Chief Justice and twenty justices, seated on Ram Shah Path, Kathmandu. It declined to release Oli and Lekhak from detention (reported 31 March 2026).

title: Telegram

description.value: Messaging app by Telegram FZ-LLC, launched 2013. It does not appear in the Kathmandu Post list of the 26 platforms blocked on 4 September 2025; no source retrieved states its status in Nepal.

title: TikTok

description.value: Video app operated by ByteDance, launched 20 September 2016. The AP reported on 4 September 2025 that TikTok and Viber were allowed to keep operating in Nepal because they had registered with the government.

title: Times Now Navbharat

description.value: Indian Hindi-language news channel. Named by Newslaundry for a foreign-hand framing of the protests and by Decode for airing old Pashupatinath footage.

title: Times of India

description.value: Indian newspaper. BOOM names it among outlets that reported the death of Ravi Laxmi Chitrakar.

title: National Trauma Centre, Kathmandu

description.value: Trauma hospital on Mahankal Marg, Kathmandu, as located in OpenStreetMap. No other source was retrieved for its description.

title: Tribhuvan University

description.value: Nepal's oldest university, founded 25 June 1959; main campus at Kirtipur.

title: Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital

description.value: Teaching hospital on Maharajgunj Road, Kathmandu, founded in 1982.

title: Tribhuvan University Institute of Medicine, forensic medicine department

description.value: Department that carried out postmortem examinations of protest victims, according to Reuters (26 September 2025).

title: Tulsipur High Court

description.value: High court whose Butwal bench ordered Rabi Lamichhane's release on bail on 18 December 2025.

title: Ujyaalo Nepal Party

description.value: Party whose chairman from 10 January 2026 is Kulman Ghising (Wikipedia).

title: UN Nepal

description.value: United Nations country presence in Nepal; its information platform at un.org.np carries UN humanitarian coordination, cluster and resource pages (accessed 2026-10-05).

title: United Nations

description.value: Intergovernmental organisation. Its Secretary-General's spokesperson, the High Commissioner for Human Rights, OHCHR spokesperson and the Resident Coordinator in Nepal each commented on the September 2025 events.

title: United States Department of State

description.value: US foreign ministry. Lowered its travel advisory for Nepal to Level 2 after the demonstrations ended.

title: Embassy of the United States in Kathmandu

description.value: US diplomatic mission. Signed the joint statement of 9 September 2025 and issued a shelter-in-place advisory to US citizens.

title: Viber

description.value: Messaging platform. Listed as registered with the ministry, so not blocked on 4 September 2025.

title: WhatsApp

description.value: Meta-owned messaging platform. Named among the platforms that did not apply to register and were blocked from 4 September 2025.

title: WION

description.value: Indian English-language news channel. Alt News says a WION journalist posted the claim that Oli never visited India as prime minister.

title: X (formerly Twitter)

description.value: Social network launched 15 July 2006, renamed X on 23 July 2023. X was among the 26 platforms blocked in Nepal in September 2025; the Kathmandu Post headline says X responded to the registration call.

title: Youth Against Corruption

description.value: Discord channel named in Wikipedia's account of the 2025 protests as one of the online groups.

title: YouTube

description.value: Video platform launched 23 April 2005, owned by Google/Alphabet. Blocked in Nepal on 4 September 2025 (AP).

title: Zee News

description.value: Indian television news channel. AFP reported that an anchor said rioters hiding in the Gen Z protest crowd tried to vandalise Pashupatinath Temple.

title: Ananda Shrestha

profile.value: Judge of the Kathmandu District Court who issued the five-day remand order for Oli and Lekhak on 29 March 2026.

title: Anil Kumar Sinha

profile.value: Former Supreme Court justice (1 August 2016-31 October 2023). Minister in the Karki interim government from 22 September 2025 to 27 March 2026, holding law, justice and parliamentary affairs and several other portfolios.

held_office.label: Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs

title: Antonio Guterres

profile.value: UN Secretary-General. A statement attributed to his spokesperson on 9 September 2025 expressed sadness at the loss of life in Nepal.

title: Anup Kumar Upadhyay

profile.value: Chief of the Ujyaalo Nepal Party, which announced unity with the RSP on 29 December 2025 and split from it on 10 January 2026.

title: Apilraj Bohora

profile.value: Kathmandu Police spokesperson (SP) at the time. Said before the protest that forces were on high alert and violators would face action.

title: Arzu Rana Deuba

profile.value: Nepali Congress. Foreign Minister from 15 July 2024 to 9 September 2025. Wikipedia reports that she and Sher Bahadur Deuba were injured and taken into police custody after their house was attacked and set on fire on 9 September 2025.

title: Asheem Man Singh Basnyat

profile.value: Then managing director of Pathao. Onlinekhabar reports he posted on the afternoon of Saturday 6 September 2025 that he would go to Maitighar on 8 September, and an intelligence report listed him as a possible participant.

title: Ashok Raj Sigdel

profile.value: Chief of the Army Staff since 9 September 2024; appointed on the Council of Ministers' recommendation and announced on 28 August 2024, succeeding Prabhu Ram Sharma. Wikipedia credits him with facilitating the dialogue between Gen Z protest leaders and the political leadership in September 2025.

title: Baburam Aryal

profile.value: Digital-law expert quoted in Nepali Times criticising the Social Media Bill as placing freedom of expression under criminal law.

title: Baburam Bhattarai

profile.value: Prime Minister 29 Aug 2011-14 Mar 2013; Finance Minister 2008-2009. Founded the Naya Shakti Party in 2016. Chairman of the Pragatisheel Loktantrik Party from 20 November 2025 (Wikipedia).

held_office.label: Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers

title: Baburam Regmi

profile.value: Former High Court judge who headed the committee that reported on 1 October 2026 on criminal cases against Gen Z protesters.

held_office.label: High-level study committee on cases against Gen Z protesters

title: Bala Nanda Sharma

profile.value: Retired Nepal Army lieutenant general who commanded the UN Disengagement Observer Force from 2004. Foreign Minister in the Karki interim government from December 2025 until 27 March 2026, when Shisir Khanal took over.

title: Balendra Shah

profile.value: Known as Balen. Elected Mayor of Kathmandu as an independent in May 2022; resigned on 18 January 2026 to contest the 5 March 2026 election. Joined the Rastriya Swatantra Party (from 28 December 2025 per Wikipedia), won Jhapa 5 defeating KP Sharma Oli, and was sworn in as Prime Minister on 27 March 2026. The Ministry of Defence and the Prime Minister's Office websites list him as Prime Minister (accessed 2026-10-05).

held_office.label: Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers

title: Beh Lih Yi

profile.value: CPJ Regional Director; quoted in the 4 September 2025 CPJ statement calling for the ban to be rescinded.

title: Bhola Nath Dhungana

profile.value: President of Digital Rights Nepal. Told AFP, as reproduced by Al Jazeera on 4 September 2025, that the sudden closure directly hits fundamental rights.

title: Bidya Bhattarai

profile.value: CPN-UML minister of education in the fourth Oli cabinet from 15 July 2024; resigned on 21 April 2025 amid differences with the prime minister and finance minister over teachers' demands, with a health reason also stated.

title: Bidya Devi Bhandari

profile.value: President of Nepal from 29 October 2015 to 13 March 2023; succeeded by Ram Chandra Paudel. Wikipedia reports that her house in Bhangal, Kathmandu, was burned during the 2025 protests.

held_office.label: Office of the President of Nepal

title: Bigyan Raj Sharma

profile.value: Former additional inspector general of police, member of the Karki inquiry commission.

member_of.label: Commission investigating the 8-9 September 2025 events (Karki commission)

title: Bijay Prasad Mishra

profile.value: Listed on Wikipedia as president of the Nepal Bar Association (accessed 2026-10-05); the date he took office is not given in the retrieved page.

title: Binod Ghimire

profile.value: Deputy Inspector General of Police and Nepal Police spokesperson. Gave Nepal Police figures on escaped prisoners and detainees in September 2025.

title: Bishnu Prasad Paudel

profile.value: CPN (UML). Deputy Prime Minister and Finance Minister from 15 July 2024. Forced out on 9 September 2025 with Oli (his own Wikipedia page); the Fourth Oli Cabinet page gives 12 September 2025 for the end of his term.

held_office.label: Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers

title: Bishowambhar Prasad Shrestha

profile.value: Chief Justice who led the Supreme Court's extended full bench in the contempt case against sidhakura.com, whose verdict required mandatory registration of online and social media platforms.

title: Bishwa Prakash Sharma

profile.value: Nepali Congress general secretary. With Gagan Thapa he demanded Home Minister Lekhak's resignation on 8 September 2025 and, on 9 September, that the party recall its ministers from the Oli government.

title: Bishweshwor Prasad Bhandari

profile.value: Legal expert, member of the Karki inquiry commission.

member_of.label: Commission investigating the 8-9 September 2025 events (Karki commission)

title: Bishwo Adhikari

profile.value: Senior Superintendent of Police and Kathmandu police chief on 8 September 2025. The Himalayan Times (10 October 2025) reports testimony that he issued the order to fire; the NHRC later recommended departmental action against a 'Senior SP Bishwa Adhikari'. The accounts are reports of testimony and recommendations, not findings of a court.
